purpose: Fingolimod is used to treat relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS) in adults and children 10 years and older. It helps reduce the number of MS flare-ups (relapses) and slows down the damage MS causes to the brain and spinal cord. It does not cure MS, but it can help you feel better and stay healthier longer.
how_it_works: Your immune system sometimes mistakenly attacks the protective coating around your nerves, which causes MS symptoms. Fingolimod works by keeping certain immune cells (called lymphocytes) trapped inside your lymph nodes so they cannot travel to your brain and spinal cord to cause damage. Think of it like redirecting troublemakers away from the area they would harm.
common_side_effects: Headache, flu-like symptoms, diarrhea, back pain, cough, and elevated liver enzymes. Some people notice their blood pressure going up slightly. You may also be more prone to catching colds or other infections since this medicine affects your immune system.
warnings: When you take your very dose, your heart rate may slow down temporarily, so your doctor will monitor you in the office for at least 6 hours. This medicine can increase your risk of serious infections, including a rare but dangerous brain infection called PML. It can also cause vision problems (macular edema), so eye exams are recommended. Do not take this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it can harm an unborn baby. Always tell your doctor about all other medicines you take.
typical_dosing: The usual dose for adults and children over 10 years old who weigh more than 40 kg (about 88 lbs) is one 0.5 mg capsule taken by mouth once a day, with or without food. Children weighing 40 kg or less take a lower dose of 0.25 mg once daily. Try to take it at the same time every day to keep it working consistently.
